pll1d32c1-d1e3501.summary: Raises the question from the teaching that the Spirit is the communion and mutual love of Father and Son: does the Father or the Son love through or by the Holy Spirit? The authorities seem to say so.

pll1d32c1-d1e3506.summary: Objection: in God loving and being are the same, since whatever seems said by quality is said by essence (Augustine). So if the Father loves through the Spirit, he would seem to be through the Spirit and to love not only by his essence but by the Gift.

pll1d32c1-d1e3526.summary: Since the question is so deep, Lombard answers only what Augustine seems to say: Father and Son love each other and keep unity not only by their essence but by their own Gift.
claims: Father and Son love by their essence and by their Gift.

pll1d32c1-d1e3533.summary: Cites De Trinitate VI: what joins both, by which the begotten is loved by the begetter and loves him, is not one of the two; they keep unity not by participation but by essence and by their own gift, not a superior's.
claims: Father and Son keep unity by their essence and their Gift.

pll1d32c1-d1e3557.summary: Cites De Trinitate XV: who would dare say the Father loves himself, the Son, or the Spirit only through the Spirit? Augustine denies that the Father loves only through the Spirit, but does not simply deny that he loves through him.
claims: The Father does not love only through the Spirit.

pl-l1d32c1.summary: Asks whether the Father or the Son loves through the Holy Spirit, since the Spirit is the love by which they love each other. The difficulty is that in God loving is being, so loving through the Spirit would seem to make the Father be through the Spirit. Lombard calls the question very deep and answers only what Augustine seems to say: Father and Son love each other and keep unity not only by their essence but by their own Gift. Augustine also denies that the Father loves only through the Spirit, without simply denying that he loves through him.
claims: The Spirit is the love by which Father and Son love each other.
Father and Son love and keep unity both by their essence and by their own Gift.
The Father does not love only through the Holy Spirit.
